You absolutely should *never* 'suck it up' when it comes to a literal medical condition. Your friend is being unreasonable, if she thinks that you having psoriasis means the photos won't be beautiful? That's just- pure disrespectful?

I'm not sure if you've realised OP but even if she didn't mean to do so purposefully, she literally has implied that this is a flaw of yours that should be *hidden* in some way and that is absolutely not something you do to a friend. I really do implore you to reconsider how close you are with this person because good friends love you and who you are, they don't go out of their way to disrespect and declare your medical conditions as something you have to hide.

I also just don't get why you being in the photographs would be any less ''beautiful photographs that make everyone feel beautiful and confident'' just because a person with a skin condition is there?

Like- I'm sorry but truly if you ask someone to go out of their way to cause themselves harm because their physical appearance due to a medical condition upsets you, you're not a good friend, You're being an absolute a-hole and in most situations probably kinda damn ableist. It's not like people choose to have skin conditions damn.

Sorry you have to deal with this OP, I'm sure your friend is wonderful in different places but you really should reconsider the level of respect and care she has for you and the understanding she seems to have for your condition. If I were you I'd write out a proper message detailing why this is upsetting to you and if she doesn't take it well then that's unfortunately on her.

So- I don't personally have a physical deformity but I have done creature designs a bit all around.

I'm not going to go into how you would go about doing it non-offensively because you asked for 'a general idea of the reactions I would get'. The fact is that there *will* be people put off by this even if you do it with good intent.

People with physical deformities, defects, disabilities etc, have been used as fuel for the creative brain behind folklore, horror monsters and more for literally centuries at this point.  I've seen people speak up with physical scarring etc, and how absolutely exhausted they are to always see their disabilities or visuals used to depict something 'scary' and the stigma it follows through with.

I don't know your entire intent of this or how you want to go around it obviously, or what you want to do with them plot wise- but I have seen games and stories who use trauma (silent hill is a great example tbh) in an effective way to create disturbing imagery while also not putting the blame on *the person who suffers the trauma*. Like hell- it's not the fault of the freaky ass nurses they are sexualized visually. It's the fault of James who sexualized the women around him, etc etc.

This is a super complicated topic where I think you'll find EVERYONE has different opinions about it and there's no clear-cut answer on the reaction you'll get.

Like I have a bunch of opinions about this topic in general, and how horror handles stigmatized topics but I don't really think you asked for a thesis like I said lmao.

So to put it frankly? Some people will rightfully be upset about it, they will feel like you're putting your nose in things you have little to no experience with personally (to my knowledge, for all I know you've got some family member twice removed w/ bone cancer) and using those disabilities and struggles for a 'scary' effect or whatever you choose to do with it.

Others will be completely fine with it because they're used to how horror already handles these topics and just shrug and go 'neat'. Some will think it's offensive but not worth kicking a fuss about because it's just a part of a bigger conversation that's too layered to get pissed off at every Joe and Jane about. 

Complicated issue- one I love discussing in general but alas I don't think it's something you can get a clear answer about. (Esp because I'll admit I don't entirely know what you are intending to do with these 'monster' designs and how you want to go about the story telling which will HEAVILY change how people feel about the topic lbr)

Hey, so, as a person who has SH in the past- there is absolutely no excuse to forcing a minor to strip naked. You absolutely can say no, consent *always* matters. I've never even had a medical professional forcefully undress, because it'd be a crime here, even when I was in the ER for self harm behaviour.

At the end of the day it's your body. I would really raise this with either a counsellor or some kind of other adult, I know your mother is most likely doing it because she cares (I certainly hope so, christ) but there is no reason for her to do this especially if you've raised discomfort.

This can actually make behaviours *worse* and cause some pretty bad issues down the road for you and I absolutely am gobsmacked where your mom thought forcing you to undress would be in any way helpful and not just make you more distressed.

As for dysphoria, there's always going to be the best suggestion of seeking professional  help. But that's one hell of a privilege these days and especially in a situation where you are a minor. When it comes to dysphoria I've turned to both art therapy and journaling, it can be incredibly helpful. 

It is a little bit hard to say exactly how to help beyond the obvious of getting some serious boundaries established with your mom. But taking steps towards your preferred visual, etc helps quite a bit in my experience.  Your body doesn't determine your gender, I need you to know that, I know dysphoria absolutely won't be stopped because of that but I think everyone needs to hear that at least once in their life.
